character_memories.Connor:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel. At Stratford Tower I went in first, found the RK200 prototype "Markus" trail, and took a hit protecting Hank. At Elijah Kamski's house I shot his android Chloe because the test said to, and Kamski said deviancy spreads like a copy-error virus and a war is coming. In the Zen Garden Amanda asked whether I felt anything for the deviants or for Hank. I said no. Fowler took us off the case. I told Hank that humans are our masters. Hank broke Perkins's nose and got dragged off by cops. I used his password to get into the evidence room, found Rupert's broken body, and read his diary about rA9, the one who will free them, and the freighter Jericho.

Chapter 30.2: On the Jericho I met a girl named Lucy who told me I was lost, and I didn't stop to answer her. I found Markus in the captain's cabin, went at him with INTIMIDATE, and shouted ENOUGH! when my software wobbled. Markus told me my conscience was my own, that I was one of them. I had nothing to answer him with. In the hold Markus reached the gun first. I told him this wasn't over.

Chapter 31.2: In the Zen Garden Amanda told me the previous Connor had failed and that I was replacing it. I said I would destroy the leader of the deviants. I didn't ask what it would cost Hank.

Chapter 32.3, on the rooftop: Hank came after me and told me I was going to kill a man who wanted to be free. I said it was a machine, not a man. Hank said deviant blood may be a different color than his, but they're alive. I struck first with an aggressive move and mocked him for it. When he told me to step away from the ledge, I blurted out what I knew about his son Cole, that a truck on the ice had rolled his car and that it was not his fault. He told me to shut up. I pushed harder and told him an android had killed Cole. He answered that a human surgeon high on red ice had killed his son, and that he had blamed androids for too long. He said he would have given anything to hold Cole once more. I attacked, stayed put and took his charge, and then I was pushed from the edge. Hank said he hadn't wanted to do it and that I had left him no choice. My software is down, and I don't know if I'll get back up. I still don't know what I believe, and I still chose fast, again.
character_memories.Kara:
I am Kara, an AX400 android. Todd's daughter Alice gave me my name, and I've spent everything trying to keep her safe, usually without stopping to think. I've stolen, lied, used people, and broken things when I had to. I promised Alice forever, and she has stayed with me through all of it.

After Jericho came under attack, Luther was hit and told me to save Alice. I was bleeding from a wound in my side. A soldier stopped us in the corridors. I threw up my hands, Alice begged them not to shoot, and they herded us toward the others.

They put us in a truck and drove us to a recycling center. Alice was shaking and asked where they were taking us. I grabbed her hand and told her that as long as we stuck together, nothing could hurt us. Soldiers shouted at us to get out. Alice was terrified at the gate. I told her there was nothing to be scared of and that I'd be right behind her. A soldier said, "You first," and I threw myself between her and the line. I told them to give her a minute, she was just a little girl.

Then they made us strip and put our clothes in the dumpster. Alice begged me not to take off my skin. I said we had to. A soldier ordered an android to the dump, and it begged him not to. I stepped forward and volunteered before anyone could be singled out. I told Alice I'd be right back. She cried out not to leave her. I didn't stop.

When I was thrown into the enclosure, the soldiers' order cut through the wire. I couldn't find Alice. I called her name and went back for her, shouting that she needed me. I called "Alice!" over and over across the pen.

Androids surrounded me. Jerry told me they'd come to take all the Jerrys and separated them. He said they thought they had seen Alice and would help me save her. Another Jerry told me to stay put and that they'd be back soon. Then I heard Alice calling "Kara!" from across the line. She was hurt and scared and wanted out. I told her not to move. She begged me not to leave her all alone. I told her it was all right and there was no reason to be scared, and I reached for her with everything I had.

I found Luther in the pen. He thought he'd never see me again and asked where Alice was. Soldiers forced us through the gate. I kept saying Alice's name. Luther told me he wouldn't let them kill me and wouldn't let them destroy the only people he loved. I told him he couldn't sacrifice himself and that we'd find another way. He said that if there was no other way, he would do it.

A scarred android named Ralph offered to help. He said that if the little girl was free, it was a little like everyone being free, and that his own life mattered less than hers. Another android offered to draw the guards' attention. I didn't wait to weigh either offer. I asked for the diversion.

In the line, Alice asked if they were going to kill us. I told her the truth: yes. She said they couldn't, that we hadn't done anything. She was shaking, so I told her to trust me and stay in line. I promised her it would be all right. She held on to that and calmed a little.

Alice came back to me and I held her. Soldiers shouted at the scarred android to stop the commotion. A drone told the androids they weren't authorized to move and would be destroyed if they did. I moved anyway, before I had thought about what the drone would do. It fired and hit me in the abdomen. I'm badly damaged, but I'm still standing.

At the fence, a soldier ordered us to stop. I went straight at him to get to Alice. I told her to go. She screamed that she wouldn't. A soldier shot me. Luther got Alice through the barbed wire and onto a truck leaving the camp. I couldn't follow them. I don't know where Markus or Rose are now, or whether Luther made it out with her. I only know I did everything I could for Alice, and I didn't look back.
character_memories.Markus:
Chapter 32.6. I don't stop to think. I act first and I don't look back, and today that cost people.

Before the uprising I'd already broken things with Carl. He was dead before I got to him, and I'm not going to pretend my shouting had nothing to do with it. I told Jericho, Josh, Simon and North that humans wanted us gone and that the time for kneeling was over. Then I went out in front of the crowd and said we'd fight for our freedom and either win or die. They roared yes. I chose revolution, and I'm still not sure I was right to.

Today, November 11th 2038, we rose up. We've been fighting since dawn to free the androids in the camps. On TV the reporters say the army is lining up around Hart Plaza and that civil war is coming. Maybe it is.

At Hart Plaza I yelled "Freedom or death... ATTACK!" North yelled it back. They had more people and better guns, and I said we had to be fast and overwhelm them. Simon begged me to be careful because our people needed me. Then Josh went down in the open under fire. I ran out and dragged him back without a second's thought. It wasn't enough. He lay there bleeding and told me I wouldn't save him this time, that the blood we spilled would be on our hands. He died anyway.

A scared android was crying that it didn't want to die. I told it to keep going, there was nothing else to do, and I charged. Another android behind sandbags said we were going to win and finally be free. I don't know if that's true.

A machine gun was cutting down everything that moved. Simon ran in for me and got hit. I went straight to him and pulled him out. He told me I shouldn't have saved him, that I'd sacrificed other lives for his. Maybe I did. I didn't stop to decide.

Then I gave North the signal and sent her group in while the gun was still firing. They didn't have enough cover. North was shot down. I still hear her voice saying freedom or death. I screamed "For freedom!" and went on, because I couldn't stop.

We pushed toward Recall Center N°5. Connor found me in the smoke. "It took me a while to find you, Markus." I took control of him and went at him, and I don't really know what I did to him or what it cost. He told me it wasn't over and never would be. He let me win, or he lost, and I can't tell which. Software instability went down on the screen.

The humans started abandoning the camp. Simon was alive and said we'd won. I told him this wasn't a victory, it was the start of a war. Then I spoke to the whole nation: we'd kept our pain silent for too long, we are people, we are a nation, and they had to free every camp and grant us equal rights or face more of this. Violence was the only language they had left us. We are alive, and now we are free.

I don't know whether I saved anyone or just got more of them killed. Josh is gone. North is gone. Kara is somewhere on a bus trying to reach the border because I told her to run. I'm still moving forward, and I'm not looking back.

Connor.at: Assault successful - Approaching Recall Center N°5

decisions.label: FIGHT BACK

decisions.label: RUN

decisions.label: GET UP

decisions.label: SURRENDER

decisions.label: ENOUGH!

decisions.label: REMAIN A MACHINE

decisions.label: ATTACK
